changes.before: Secondary two-sided matched-block comparisons used separate fixed Holm families: eight fault tests comparing SysRq and SIGKILL with QMP for each key; eight block-state tests comparing logging and drop-writes with linear control; twelve environment tests comparing three alternatives with custom ext4; and twelve workload tests comparing three alternatives with quiet reference. No formal trace or byte-capture test was added. The minimum attainable unadjusted two-sided p-value with ten discordant pairs is 0.001953125. At the first Holm rank, the corresponding minima are 0.005859375 for a three-test family, 0.015625 for eight tests, and 0.0234375 for twelve. The 20-pair grid contrast can reach 0.00000190735 unadjusted; nine pairs can reach only 0.00390625. These are attainability limits, not power estimates.
changes.after: Secondary two-sided matched-block comparisons used separate fixed Holm families: eight fault tests comparing SysRq and SIGKILL with QMP for each key; eight block-state tests comparing logging and drop-writes with linear control; twelve environment tests comparing three alternatives with custom ext4; and twelve workload tests comparing three alternatives with quiet reference. No formal trace or byte-capture test was added. Family sizes and minimum attainable p-values are retained in the supplementary statistical details; missing pairs did not reduce a registered family size.

changes.before: Risk differences were alternative minus reference recovery proportion. Their pointwise 95% intervals used Newcombe method 10, combining the two marginal Wilson-score intervals without continuity correction [29]. This construction was not a paired or block-adjusted confidence interval; the paired randomization test and the marginal descriptive interval answer different statistical questions. We neither used its exclusion of zero as a multiplicity decision nor treated it as a simultaneous interval. The full grid and all nonsignificant secondary cells remained descriptive. A post hoc analysis ranked achieved intervals in the twenty assigned-2.0-s trials, conditional on the observed three recovery labels. All 1,140 pooled allocations and 450 allocations preserving recovery counts within close strata were enumerated. This exploratory outcome-label permutation adds exchangeability assumptions; it is not the registered blocked binary test. It neither changed a multiplicity family nor estimated a deterministic threshold. The inventory totals of recovered and lost observations were not converted into a pooled recovery rate because the chosen condition mixture determines that aggregate.
changes.after: Risk differences were alternative minus reference recovery proportion. Pointwise Newcombe method 10 intervals combined marginal Wilson-score intervals without continuity correction [29]; they did not adjust for pairing or multiplicity. The paired exact tests supplied the primary inference. Full primary intervals appear in Supplementary Table S7. The full grid and nonsignificant secondary cells remained descriptive. The post hoc assigned-2.0-s rank analysis is reported only in the supplement and neither changed the registered tests nor fitted a threshold. Inventory totals were not converted to a pooled recovery rate.

changes.before: The dedicated key comparison exposed an ordering reversal with respect to ACK age: immediate close at a 2.50 s host-ACK deadline recovered 10/10, while delayed close at a later 2.75 s deadline recovered 0/10. Every matched pair differed, giving Holm p = 0.00390625 (Table 2). Thus a longer ACK-based wait did not order recovery monotonically across these two connection policies. The registered test did not fix the expected direction, so this is two-sided evidence of a difference rather than confirmation of a prespecified sign.

changes.before: Before and at the ACK marker, all forty dependent logging prefixes lacked the target. The final recorded prefix, also the last recorded FLUSH-or-FUA event, recovered 10/10 after immediate close, 0/10 after delayed close, 0/10 when held 5 s, and 2/10 when held 15 s. New recovery of all forty literal last-FLUSH prefixes gave the same cell counts: 10/10, 0/10, 0/10, and 2/10, with no unknown derived endpoints (Supplementary Table S6). In thirty-nine logs this literal prefix omits one final 4096-byte FUA metadata record; one log already ends with FLUSH plus FUA. The literal prefix was therefore read independently rather than inheriting the final-prefix oracle. The capture log establishes recorded event order, not exact completion times. A flush/FUA issue in one held-15-s capture overlaps the controller dispatch/quiesce uncertainty. These reconstructions characterize logged disk-state prefixes; they do not reproduce physical cache loss at an instantaneous fault. The pre-ACK prefixes remain preconditions rather than acknowledged losses.

changes.before: Workload cells recovered 10/10 after immediate close for quiet, background-fsync, and ten-record transactions, but 0/10 with four connections (Figure 6). The latter contrast had Holm p = 0.0234375. Delayed-close and held-5-s cells were 0/10 for every workload. Held-15-s recovery was 3/10 for quiet, 4/10 with background fsync, 4/10 with ten records, and 1/10 with four connections. Those differences did not pass the workload correction. No eligible ten-record endpoint was partially recovered.
changes.after: Retaining three additional connections eliminated immediate-close recovery in the observed workload cells: 0/10 recovered with four connections, compared with 10/10 for the quiet reference (Figure 6; Holm p = 0.0234375). Background-fsync and ten-record immediate-close cells also recovered 10/10. This contrast is consistent with recovery being associated with release of the last usable connection, without identifying the causal cleanup event. Delayed-close and held-5-s cells were 0/10 for every workload. Held-15-s recovery was 3/10 for quiet, 4/10 with background fsync, 4/10 with ten records, and 1/10 with four connections. Those differences did not pass correction. No eligible ten-record endpoint was partially recovered.

changes.before: The trace family yielded 4/4, 0/3, 0/5, and 1/4 eligible recoveries for the four keys. Three acknowledged endpoints were unknown and one slot had no ACK. For delayed close, recovered/ACK was 0/5, with missing-endpoint bounds of 0–40%; for held 15 s it was 1/5, with bounds of 20–40%. Immediate-close recovery was 4/4 acknowledged trials from five assignments; the unmeasured slot was not an acknowledged loss. The 16 eligible traces reported no buffer data loss, but tracing was deliberately ended about 0.5 s before dispatch. Events in that final window were outside coverage. These observations were descriptive and did not establish callback attribution.
changes.after: The trace family yielded 4/4, 0/3, 0/5, and 1/4 eligible recoveries for the four keys. Three acknowledged endpoints were unknown and one slot had no ACK. For delayed close, recovered/ACK was 0/5, with missing-endpoint bounds of 0–40%; for held 15 s it was 1/5, with bounds of 20–40%. Immediate-close recovery was 4/4 acknowledged trials from five assignments; the unmeasured slot was not an acknowledged loss. The 16 eligible traces reported no buffer data loss. Trace acquisition was ended approximately 0.5 s before fault dispatch. Delayed-close trace end requests occurred 1.247–1.254 s after close, before the approximately 2 s candidate cleanup interval. Immediate-close end requests occurred 2.001–2.009 s after close, near that interval; the traces cannot be described as uniformly excluding it. The final pre-fault window was outside declared coverage, and the enabled categories supplied no direct callback marker. These observations were descriptive and did not establish callback attribution.

changes.after: The two-second constant and this Release/self-destruction control path were still present on the inspected main revision, committed 6 October 2026 [30]. Other parts of the file had changed; we do not claim complete implementation identity or that current main reproduces the measured outcomes. A packaged binary was used throughout, and no source-built instrumentation or runtime callback marker was added. The bounded category traces omitted the final half-second and did not directly identify the candidate callback. Byte capture did not resolve target serialization, and the supporting syscall traces identified WAL activity rather than the invoked Chromium function. Consequently callback attribution remains not established. Filesystem writeback, SQLite synchronization and checkpointing, scheduling, and cleanup can contribute overlapping effects that this design does not separate.

changes.before: The study tested whether connection lifetime and specified fault scope conditioned recovery of acknowledged writes in one pinned SQLite-backed IndexedDB configuration. The prospective 930-slot design was consumed without replacing failures; 925 slots yielded eligible complete/absent endpoints.
changes.after: Connection lifetime conditioned recovery of acknowledged relaxed transactions in this pinned, forced-SQLite IndexedDB stack. The campaign consumed 930 assignments without replacing failures and yielded 925 eligible endpoints. The close-aligned endpoint contrast and immediate-versus-delayed-close comparison passed primary Holm correction; held 15 s versus held 5 s did not. Secondary comparisons distinguished browser termination from guest reboot and showed reduced immediate-close recovery under early post-ACK write dropping or retention of additional connections.

changes.before: Two primary comparisons passed Holm correction: the close-aligned 2.4-versus-1.6 s endpoint contrast and the immediate-versus-delayed-close ordering comparison. Held 15 s versus held 5 s did not. Secondary comparisons distinguished SIGKILL from QMP reset for delayed and held connections, and showed lower immediate-close recovery with drop-writes or three additional retained connections. The source-supported two-second release path was consistent with the pattern, but runtime callback attribution remains unestablished. Early silent dropping was a post-ACK write-cutoff intervention; its target-bearing sector sequence remains unassigned. Log-prefix reconstructions were dependent observations, not new trials or physical cache-loss tests.
changes.after: The registered results, separately reported supporting WAL syscall observations and pinned source path are consistent with recovery following release of the last usable connection, while allowing a different route for held-open recovery. This interpretation remains a hypothesis: runtime callback attribution and the target-bearing page/sector sequence are not established. Completion, connection policy, backend and fault scope must therefore remain distinct in recovery testing. These configuration-specific findings provide no safe waiting time, physical-power guarantee or portability claim.
